info.name: OnChainRisk API
info.description:
ONE collection for the whole API, used with EITHER the **OnChainRisk Production** or the **OnChainRisk Sandbox** environment. The credential is the only thing that changes: same requests, same paths, same bodies, same client code. Load an environment, put your key in `api_key`, and run.

Both environments declare exactly the same variable NAMES, so nothing here can depend on which one is loaded. Where the two tiers genuinely behave differently — the two Telegram operations, which a sandbox credential is documented to refuse — the test script reads `tier` and asserts the right outcome. The requests themselves never branch.

Sandbox requests reach the same paths and return the same shapes; execution is simulated or served from committed fixtures, and nothing is billed. See `integration/capability-matrix.md` for the per-operation mode.

The reference document is https://api.onchainrisk.io/openapi.yaml for production and https://api.onchainrisk.io/openapi-sandbox.yaml for the sandbox — two views of the same 45 operations.

**Public Share Links (no auth).** `GET /api/share/{token}` and `GET /api/share/{token}/graph` send no `Authorization` header: the share token *is* the credential, and the report owner gave you that token. Do not add a paid key to them: the remaining operations inherit the collection bearer, and these two deliberately override it to `noauth`.

Folders group by tag, and they are safe day-to-day except where a request says otherwise: `Analysis`, `Multi-Chain`, `Account`, `AI Investigation`, `Watchlist`, `Labels`, `Notifications`, `Graph`, `Sharing`, `Saved Reports`.

Generated from `web/api/contract/*` by `scripts/generate-postman-collection.mjs`. Do not edit by hand — a hand edit is overwritten by the next generation and fails the canonical check.

request.description:
Analyze address risk

Answers **200** with the finished report when the scan completes inline, or **202** with `reportId` and `status` when it goes asynchronous — read the status code, not the body shape. On 202, poll `GET /api/v1/check/status/{reportId}` until `complete` or `failed`; this request captures the id for you. Validation failures are always **422** with `success: false` and `error.code = VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Sandbox: the documented FIXTURE input is `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735735` on `eth` — the value this environment already supplies — and returns a deterministic fixture report. Two further documented inputs exercise the async lifecycle instead: `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735a01` (completes) and `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735f01` (fails). Paste one into `sample_address` to take that path. Every other address is SIMULATED.

exec: pm.test('reportId captured for the status and fetch requests', () => pm.expect(d.reportId).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Analyze address risk (GET)

Async scan status (polling)

Lightweight polling for the async path. Lifecycle: `queued` → `analyzing` → `complete` | `failed`. Does NOT consume quota. Poll every ~5 seconds; a heavy address typically takes 1–5 minutes. `sample_report_id` is captured for you by `POST /api/v1/check` when that call answers 202.

request.description:
Full multi-chain risk analysis

The full cross-chain analysis. `networks` must be NON-EMPTY — an empty array is 422 — so this request sends `["{{sample_network}}"]`; add more slugs from the capability matrix. Answers **202** with an INTEGER `reportId`, captured into `sample_multichain_analysis_id` for the progress poll. That integer is NOT a report id: the saved multi-chain report is a UUID, and the scan above captures that one. Costs more than a single-chain check.

item.name: Public report view by share token

request.description:
Public report view by share token

Takes **no credential** — the collection-level bearer is deliberately overridden to `noauth` here, because the contract says this operation is public. Anyone holding the token can read the report.

item.name: Public graph view by share token

request.description:
Public graph view by share token

Takes **no credential**, like its sibling. Treat a share token as a secret: it is the only thing standing between a reader and the report.

Save a token security report

`reportPublicId` is OPTIONAL and is the idempotency key. Supply a stable UUID you generate yourself and a retry after a timeout answers **200** with `duplicate: true` and `charged: false` instead of saving and charging twice. Omit it and the server mints one, returned as `data.id` — that path is **not** retry-safe. `data.id` is that public UUID, which is NOT the integer `id` the list returns.
List saved token reports

Save a block analysis (MEV) report

RESOLVES the report `POST /api/v1/block/analyze` already saved — it does not create one, and `reportData` is ignored. Supply `reportPublicId` (preferred, and what this request sends) or `reportId`; with neither, both `blockNumber` and `network` are required and the analysis is found through a short-lived per-account cache. With nothing identifying at all the answer is 422. A truthy `name` renames the resolved report, truncated at 200 characters.

exec: // Resolves the report the analyze call already saved, by the id it captured.
// Now DECLARED statuses, not an allowlist against a silent contract: 404 not-found/
// not-owned, 410 legacy-or-deleted correlation, 422 nothing identifying supplied.
pm.test('a documented non-success, not a surprise', () => pm.expect([404, 410, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code));
